## Three things that matter

1. **TSMC's 53% August revenue surge validates the AI infrastructure supercycle thesis**
This is the clearest real-money signal in semis this week — not guidance, not backlog, actual recognized revenue up 53% YoY. For bankers, it anchors valuation multiples for any AI chip or foundry-adjacent equity story and supports the bull case on Oracle's capex-driven server pull-through (HPE +11%, Dell +11%, Super Micro +7% on Oracle's raised capex guidance).

2. **Anthropic and OpenAI face compounding regulatory pressure that clouds near-term capital events**
Claude's reported use in guided weapons development and Senator Hawley's public "reckless conduct" accusation against OpenAI are occurring simultaneously, just as Congressional doomsday warnings dominate the Hill. Both companies have active or anticipated fundraising needs; a deteriorating regulatory backdrop raises cost of capital and complicates governance diligence for any lead investor.

3. **Oracle's $664B backlog is converting — Citi calls the overhang gone**
Analyst commentary that a major overhang has lifted, combined with AI metrics Wall Street is treating as a revenue inflection signal, sets up a potential institutional re-rating. Relevant for comps across cloud/infrastructure software and for any debt financing tied to Oracle's elevated capex commitments.

## Deal flow

The DOJ probe into Nvidia's ~$20B Groq acquisition is the headline risk — antitrust scrutiny on the dominant AI accelerator player could set precedent for the broader sector. ADI's $1.35B Alif Semiconductor deal and Samsung's acquisition of cooling specialist Flakt both reflect strategic edge-AI and data center infrastructure buildout. Bending Spoons acquiring Miro at a ~90% discount to 2022 peak valuation is a pointed reminder of late-stage startup markdown risk. Pasqal filed an F-1 for a US quantum computing IPO under ticker PSQL.

## Watching

Qualcomm is spiking at 29x its weekly average on the Amazon partnership news — watch for read-through to AI inference silicon alternatives to Nvidia. Samsung Electronics is running at 21x average mention volume; between the Flakt acquisition and ongoing foundry competition, it warrants close attention into next week. Nscale and Upstage are both signaling pre-IPO positioning, suggesting the data center and AI infrastructure IPO pipeline is quietly building.

## Three things that matter

1. **Broadcom's 2028 guidance and memory's Goldman-called bottom reset the semiconductor valuation floor.** Broadcom's rare multi-year forward guidance signals durable AI chip and networking revenue visibility — a direct comp anchor for any semis M&A or debt deal. Separately, Goldman calling the memory downcycle bottom sent SK Hynix ADRs to record highs (+5%), SanDisk +3%, and Micron +2%; with S&P flagging a potential 40 trillion won SK Hynix buyback in Q4, capital return capacity at the memory majors is now a live conversation.

2. **China stockpiled ASML scanners, leaving a servicing ban as the only remaining export-control lever.** This materially narrows Western regulators' toolkit and extends the timeline for constraining CXMT and YMTC — a direct headwind to KLA's export-exposed revenue (KLAC fell 3.82% on September 9 on related concerns). For deal work, any semis target with China fab exposure faces a widening regulatory risk discount.

3. **Anthropic's existential-risk commentary and researcher resignations are a regulatory flashpoint for AI lab valuations.** A safety lead publicly assigning >10% human-extinction odds, combined with a researcher resignation citing reckless development pace, creates a credible near-term catalyst for legislative action. For AI lab financings and secondaries, buyers should stress-test governance structures and liability frameworks now.

## Deal flow

Nvidia is the dominant acquirer on the tape with a reported $12.9B acquisition of an unnamed OpenAI-associated AI startup, a strategic investment in Hugging Face at a $12.93B valuation, and a separate $2.5B position in Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab — plus nearly $13B deployed into an AI developer platform. The Amazon/Qualcomm structure ($4B equity stake tied to a custom AI chip supply agreement) is pending. Nscale is in talks for $3.5B in pre-IPO financing backed by a $45B Anthropic supply deal. Oura filed its S-1 on September 3 with no pricing disclosed.

## Watching

SK Hynix and Samsung are both spiking hard (scores of 20x and 32x above baseline, respectively) — watch for any foundry or HBM supply announcement as an immediate catalyst. Corporate AI adoption slowed in August as token prices fell, which tension-tests the hyperscaler capex narratives from Amazon, Meta, and Google heading into Q3 earnings season.

## Three things that matter

1. **Qualcomm-Amazon custom silicon deal reshapes the hyperscaler chip competitive map.**
Qualcomm surged ~9-10% on a multi-generation agreement to design custom AI data center chips for Amazon, accompanied by a $4B equity stake transfer and a warrant for up to 25 million shares — a structure that ties customer and supplier economics tightly together. For coverage, this is a direct comp read-through to Broadcom and Marvell on hyperscaler ASIC economics, and the $60B milestone revenue ceiling makes this one of the largest disclosed silicon supply arrangements on record.

2. **China's 70% control of a critical AI datacenter material crystallizes supply-chain risk for semis.**
The concentration exposes the entire AI infrastructure buildout to potential export-control escalation, which layers onto Ontario's new 50% retaliatory tariffs on U.S. electronics — a compounding cross-border cost shock. Analysts modeling Nvidia, ASML, and memory names need to stress-test procurement assumptions; any escalation could reprice capex timelines for hyperscalers.

3. **Intel's 5-6% single-day move warrants M&A and foundry re-rating scrutiny.**
The catalyst is dual: High-NA EUV fabrication progress (ASML linkage) and a Trump social-media post that implies potential policy tailwinds for domestic foundry. A planned ~10% CPU price hike in October adds a near-term margin catalyst. Any policy-driven subsidy acceleration or strategic review would move Intel's foundry-services valuation materially.

## 오늘의 핵심 3가지

1. **앤트로픽의 2조 달러 기업공개(IPO)는 AI 역사상 가장 중요한 공모 — 거버넌스 구조가 핵심 변수.** 동사는 민간 자본 1,300억 달러를 조달하고 스페이스엑스(SpaceX) 구조를 모델로 한 150억 달러 규모의 리볼빙 크레딧 시설을 마련해 공모 시점 조율을 위한 충분한 runway를 확보하였습니다. 이중 미션 거버넌스에 내재된 외부 수탁자(external trustee) 구조는 공개시장 투자자 및 인수단의 집중 심사를 받을 전망이며, 통제권 프리미엄 할인율 산정에 직접 영향을 미칩니다. 레버리지 ETF 신청(ANUU/ANDD)은 매수 측이 이미 포지셔닝에 나섰음을 시사합니다.

2. **엔비디아의 AI 자본 집행은 일회성이 아닌 구조적 현상 — 1년간 주식 투자 990억 달러.** 현재 검토 중인 딜로는 미라 무라티(Mira Murati)의 Thinking Machines Lab에 대한 25억 달러 투자 및 미디어텍(MediaTek)에 대한 35억 달러 전환사채(CB) 투자가 보고되고 있으며, 공급망 전반에 걸쳐 전략적 영향력을 중첩 확대하는 구도입니다. 에코시스템 잠금(lock-in)에 투입된 것으로 알려진 130억 달러는 해자(moat) 논거를 강화하는 동시에, 투자 범위 확대에 따른 반독점 노출 면적을 키웁니다.

3. **존 테너스(John Ternus)로의 애플 최고경영자 교체, 세계 최대 하드웨어 기업의 재평가 논쟁 점화.** 동시에 발표된 홈 보안·모니터링 서비스 출시 계획은 테너스가 서비스 부문 성장 유지를 위해 반복 매출 수직계열화를 더욱 강하게 밀어붙일 것임을 시사합니다. 애플 공급업체 및 인접 보안기술 기업 담당 뱅커들은 테너스가 전략적 우선순위를 확립하는 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 인수합병(M&A) 활동을 모델에 반영해야 합니다.

## 딜 동향

엔비디아가 복수의 투자 건으로 시장을 주도하고 있습니다: Thinking Machines Lab에 대한 25억 달러 투자, 미디어텍에 대한 35억 달러 규모 CB 투자, 그리고 가치 미공개의 Hugging Face 전략적 투자가 추진 중입니다. Flex의 EPC Power 44억 달러 인수는 AI 데이터센터 전력 인프라 수요를 겨냥하며 현재 심사 중입니다. Oura Inc.는 9월 3일 S-1을 제출하였으나 공모가는 미공개입니다. Palo Alto Networks는 Console 인수(5억 달러)를 완료하였습니다.

## 관전 포인트

카카오, SK텔레콤, KT 등 국내 통신주가 최근 거의 바닥에 가까운 기저에서 일제히 급등 중입니다. 한국 AI 또는 규제 관련 촉매의 존재 여부를 주시하시기 바랍니다. 오라클(Oracle) 실적은 단기 반도체·클라우드 촉매로, 옵션 시장은 11% 이상의 주가 변동을 가격에 반영하고 있으며 VA(버지니아주) 계약 확대 소식은 이미 신규 목표주가 산정으로 이어지고 있습니다. 피차이(Pichai)가 언급한 웨이모(Waymo)의 2027년 손익기여(contribution) 타임라인은 연말까지 알파벳(Alphabet)의 재평가를 이끌 수 있는 잠재적 변수입니다.
